headline: GOLD SINKS TO $4,332 AS SAUDI PIPELINE SHUTDOWN SENDS OIL NEAR $108 — PRECIOUS METALS SQUEEZED ON BOTH SIDES BEFORE FED
snippet: Saudi Arabia suspended its 7-million-barrel-per-day East-West pipeline after drone attacks in the Riyadh and Madinah regions Monday, sending Brent to $107.95 and WTI to $103.19. Gold fell to $4,332 (down $37) and silver broke below $64 support to $63.35. With the Fed meeting September 15-16 and an 86% priced-in rate hike, rising oil prices — inflationary and thus pro-tightening — create a second headwind for precious metals exactly when the sector needed macro tailwinds.

headline: BANNERMAN LOCKS IN A$124M AND CHINESE NUCLEAR PARTNER FOR ETANGO — FID Q4 2026, SETTLEMENT TOMORROW
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) has closed a fully underwritten A$124M placement at A$4.00/share — settling September 15 — fully funding its share of the Etango uranium project in Namibia through construction and ramp-up. China National Nuclear Corporation's offshore arm, CNNC Overseas (CNOL), holds 45% of the joint venture with Bannerman retaining 55%. Final investment decision and full construction start are targeted Q4 2026. Uranium spot holds near $90/lb as 38 nations pursue a tripling of nuclear capacity.

headline: SILVER BREAKS $64 SUPPORT AT $63.35 — FED HIKE BETS AND SAUDI OIL SHOCK CREATE RARE DUAL-PRESSURE EVENT
snippet: Silver dropped to $63.35 on September 14, breaking below the $64 level analysts had flagged as the threshold between healthy correction and structural weakness. The metal faces a rare simultaneous headwind: an 86% priced-in Fed rate hike on Tuesday, plus surging oil prices from the Saudi pipeline shutdown adding inflationary pressure that perversely supports tightening. Silver's industrial demand from solar, EV, and AI data-centre infrastructure remains structurally intact, but near-term macro pressure is dominating price action.

headline: BRENT PAST $108: HORMUZ WAR AND SAUDI PIPELINE SHUTDOWN EFFECTIVELY CLOSE GULF OIL ROUTES — ENERGY COST SHOCK FOR MINERS
snippet: Brent crude surged past $108/bbl after Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline — its critical non-Hormuz alternative — while simultaneous Strait of Hormuz disruptions have blocked more than 10 million barrels per day of Gulf output. HSBC had already raised its Brent target to $90 last week on Hormuz risk; actual prices now run well above that. For miners, diesel accounts for 15-20% of cash costs at most open-pit operations: a sustained oil price above $100/bbl in Q4 will pressure margins at gold and copper producers already navigating a rate-hike environment.

headline: COPPER FALLS TO $6.40/LB ON SAUDI RISK-OFF — FIRST LOSING WEEK SINCE JUNE DESPITE TIGHTENING SUPPLY
snippet: Copper fell to $6.40/lb (US$14,122/t) on September 14, down 1.0% on the day, capping its first losing week since June after closing at $14,233 on Friday. The pullback from the record $14,875 high accelerated after the White House shelved its Section 232 copper tariff recommendation; Monday's Saudi pipeline shock added a risk-off tone across base metals. The fundamental picture remains tight: Codelco and Freeport-McMoRan both posted double-digit H1 production declines and a global 1.1% drop in output was flagged by the International Copper Study Group.

headline: BOSS ENERGY HONEYMOON: 13.8M LB U3O8 MINE PLAN, FY27 GUIDANCE AT 1.25-1.30M LBS — TWO YEARS OF REAL DATA REPLACE ASSUMPTIONS
snippet: Boss Energy has published an updated economic life-of-mine plan for its Honeymoon ISR uranium project in South Australia, projecting 13.8 million pounds U3O8 over a nine-year operating period — figures drawn from two years of real production data since the April 2024 restart rather than pre-production assumptions. FY2027 guidance is set at 1.25–1.30 million pounds. Total estimated resources stand at 20.8 million pounds U3O8 at a 100 ppm cut-off, with 13.7 million pounds in the indicated category.

headline: STANMORE ADDS 724MT GOONYELLA COKING COAL RESOURCE FOR $US105M — MORANBAH SOUTH ROUNDS OUT BOWEN BASIN POSITION
snippet: Stanmore Resources has agreed to acquire the Moranbah South metallurgical coal tenements in Queensland from Exxaro Resources for US$105 million, adding 724 million tonnes of measured and indicated Goonyella Middle Seam premium hard coking coal directly adjacent to the company's Eagle Downs and Isaac Downs Extension projects. The deal follows a complex ownership chain: Exxaro exercised pre-emptive rights after Anglo American's Australian coal assets were sold to Dhilmar. Completion targeted Q4 2026, subject to FIRB, ACCC, and ministerial approvals.

headline: SPROTT MONEY SEPTEMBER OUTLOOK: GOLD BULL FLAG OR BEAR BOUNCE — THE FED BINARY DECIDES THIS WEEK
snippet: Chris Vermeulen's September 2026 technical read for Sprott Money frames gold's current position as a critical juncture: short-term momentum has turned bullish after three down weeks from the $4,691 August high, but the longer-term structure still shows lower highs and lower lows. The $4,264 zone is the line — hold and the correction becomes a textbook wave-2 pullback before a third-wave advance; break and $4,200 becomes the next target. Gold miners up 50% from July lows are leading every corrective leg, consistent with the early stages of a primary advance.

headline: KAISER RESEARCH: JUNIOR MINERS PAUSE FOR FED — FINANCING VOLUMES STAY HIGH AS SECTOR WAITS FOR BINARY WEEK TO PASS
snippet: Kaiser Research's September 11 weekly frames the junior sector pause ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC as consolidation within a structurally sound bull market rather than a breakdown. TSX and TSX-V equity financing through July reached $10.1 billion — near a decade high — with mining companies accounting for roughly half. Specific catalysts are generating capital attention: Bannerman's uranium FID, Faraday Copper's Arizona district play, and a cluster of gold explorers in Northern Ontario. The Fed binary is creating an entry window, historically a better-performing setup than chasing after the decision.

headline: RARE EARTHS: NOVEMBER 10 CHINA EXPORT PAUSE EXPIRY IS THE NEXT BILLION-DOLLAR BINARY — THREE SCENARIOS, ONE DOMINANT SUPPLIER
snippet: Mining Stock Education's September analysis argues the November 10 expiry of China's rare earth export suspension is the clearest sector catalyst on the calendar. Three scenarios are priced: extension of the pause, selective reinstatement for allied nations, or full reimposition of controls. China controls 69% of mine production and ~90% of processing — any reimposition triggers re-rating of Western rare earth developers with proven deposits and processing infrastructure, including MP Materials, USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels, and the pipeline of Australian and Canadian projects being built specifically to reduce China dependency.
